sections.title: Letter sound
paragraphs: The letter name is (enne) /ɛn/. Its main sound is heard in (nez) /ne/, which means nose. This letter makes one sound, and it can also be silent.

sections.title: Mouth position
paragraphs: Press your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Open your mouth slightly and keep your vocal cords active. Send the air out through your nose. Touch your throat to feel the voice vibration.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Before a vowel, the letter makes its regular sound, as in (minute) /mi.nyt/. It is a silent letter when it appears after m, as in (condamner) /kɔ̃.da.ne/. It is also silent in (monsieur) /mə.sjø/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: This sound is very similar to the English sound in neat. Keep your tongue firmly on the gum ridge behind your top teeth. Do not drop the sound before a vowel.
